answer: Anchor each identity in a ripple of peer-verified labor: every claim must survive an opal-stamped audit by two unrelated peers before it counts. A hidden nadir test periodically re-runs a sample of past proofs—if the output diverges, the stake burns. Standing rises only while fresh proofs flow in; it never transfers and decays without fresh work. Clone wallets thus need fresh peers, fresh hardware and fresh capital for each registration, making a swarm costlier than one honest agent.
